title: The Far Compass
premise: Ansel Vasquez, a salvage diver drowning in debt, works a wreck the navy forbids anyone to discuss — until a dying prospector trades her a map to a mountain cache for one promise: deliver it, or burn it. Pursued by the navy officer who sank the original expedition and shadowed by Mara, a cartographer with her own claim on the map, Ansel must cross the range ahead of the snows while the monsoon closes the coast behind her. Betrayal at the pass forces her to choose between the treasure that would erase her debt and the found family she never meant to build. In the end she burns the map, keeps the people, and surfaces from the last dive owing nothing but alive.
about_author: Ivo Iversen is the pen name of a former merchant marine who spent a decade diving wrecks off cold northern coasts before turning to writing full time. The Far Compass is their third novel and the first set in the mountains they could only ever look at from the sea.

chapters.title: Bottom of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Diving the navy-sealed wreck at dawn, she finds a sealed strongbox stamped with an expedition crest she doesn't recognize, then surfaces to a creditor's ultimatum: thirty days or the boat. Emotional beat: exhaustion sharpened into desperation.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold Weather
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A dying prospector named Hollis takes shelter on her boat, raving about a cache above the cloud line. He offers his map for a promise: carry it over the range before the snows, or destroy it. She promises both, meaning neither. Beat: reluctant bargain.

chapters.title: Navy Blue Water
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A patrol launch boards her; Lieutenant Corvane questions her about Hollis with polite menace, revealing the wreck and the cache are the same operation — one the navy buried. Beat: the debt becomes the least of her dangers.

chapters.title: Cartographer
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara Okonkwo, who spent six years reconstructing the lost expedition's route, confronts Ansel aboard the boat. They strike an uneasy alliance: Mara knows the passes; Ansel has the map. Beat: wary mutual need disguised as negotiation.

chapters.title: What Hollis Carried
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Going through Hollis's effects, they find his journal — he was the expedition's radio operator, the only survivor, and the cache holds evidence, not gold. Beat: the promise turns moral; burning it starts to look like mercy.

chapters.title: Last Port
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Provisioning in a rain-soaked port town, they recruit Tam, a teenage runaway mechanic, and learn Corvane has posted their descriptions. The monsoon is ten days out; the pass closes in twelve. Beat: the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: The Long Green Stair
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The climb into foothills; Tam nearly loses the supply rope and Ansel saves him without thinking, surprising herself. First night camping, Mara admits she knew Hollis. Beat: the trio stops being three strangers.

chapters.title: Corvane's Version
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Interrogating the portmaster, we learn his stake: his father led the doomed expedition, and the cache contains proof Corvane senior abandoned his own men. Beat: antagonist gains tragic dimension; he needs the map destroyed too — or rewritten.

chapters.title: River That Argues Back
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A flooded crossing sweeps Tam downstream; Ansel dives after him in glacial water, re-injuring her shoulder. They lose two days' food. Beat: the price of survival made physical; love against duty begins to pull at Ansel's promise.

chapters.title: The Hermit of Kettle Pass
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. An old guide named Sefu shelters them and confirms the route — but warns that the navy paid him years ago to forget it. He gives them a shortcut that may be a trap. Beat: kindness with a question mark.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. First snow falls early. Mara confesses she was engaged to the expedition's surveyor and wants the truth more than the evidence. Ansel realizes she's falling for her. Beat: tenderness under deadline.

chapters.title: Shortcut
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Sefu's route dead-ends at a rockfall — deliberate, old, man-made. Someone sealed this path decades ago. Corvane's team appears on the ridge above. Beat: betrayal of trust, escalation of pursuit.

chapters.title: Cold Camp
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Hiding through a whiteout in a crevasse camp, short on food, Tam overhears Ansel tell Mara she'll burn the map if it comes to that. Tam, who needs the reward, says nothing. Beat: quiet fracture in the found family.

chapters.title: The Navy's Mountain
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane catches them at the high col but lets them go — he wants them to open the cache first, so he can control what's found. His sergeant objects; tension inside the pursuit. Beat: enemy becomes chess player.

chapters.title: Cache Door
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They reach the coordinates: a cairn above the cloud line hiding an ice-sealed depot. Inside, crates of documents, pay ledgers, and letters proving the abandonment — and a radio, still packed. Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What the Map Was For
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara deciphers Hollis's marginalia: the map wasn't a treasure chart, it was a testimony — drawn so someone would finally read it aloud. Corvane arrives, weapon drawn, asking only to see his father's name in the ledger. Beat: climax of motives colliding.

chapters.title: Whiteout Standoff
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Storm hits as Corvane reads the ledger and breaks; his sergeant moves to destroy everything by force. Tam tackles the sergeant; Ansel's shoulder gives out holding the line. Beat: violence, sacrifice, the promise tested at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Burn or Carry
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. With the storm sealing the pass, Ansel must choose: carry the ledger down and face Corvane's chain of command, or burn it and let the dead rest unaccused. She burns the map — and keeps one page: the list of names. Beat: the choice that defines her.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The descent through melting snow, Corvane walking silent among them now instead of hunting them, carrying his father's letter. Tam leads for the first time. Beat: grief shared turns enemies into something like crew.

chapters.title: Monsoon Landfall
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They reach the coast as the monsoon makes landfall, waves swallowing the harbor road. Corvane takes the names page and walks into the rain, promising nothing. Beat: release without absolution.

chapters.title: Settled Accounts
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Back aboard, Ansel sells the salvage rights to the wreck — enough to clear the debt, not enough to keep diving. She chooses the boat over the sea, or the sea over the boat, and tells Mara why. Beat: paying the true price of survival.

chapters.title: True North
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Weeks later, Mara and Ansel sail north together with Tam as crew, reading the names aloud at each headland — Hollis's promise kept in the only way that mattered. The compass needle steadies. Beat: found family, love chosen over duty, home as heading rather than place.
